text:
The gain failure comes from the feedback network, not the amplifier core. With the op-amp's loop gain high, the closed-loop gain is set by 1 + Rf/Rg. Here that gives 1 + 1227/2528.2 ≈ 1.485, close to the measured 1.458. The spec needs 0.9–1.1, so Rf/Rg must be about 0 to 0.1.

Bandwidth and offset pass, and the sensitivities confirm that a1 depends mainly on Rf and Rg. The M5 triode condition is real and worth fixing, but it doesn't explain the gain error. Its effect is on the tail current and input-pair headroom, not on the ratio that sets gain.

Rg is the most likely corrupted element. A value near 25 kΩ (about 10× the current 2.5 kΩ) would give a gain of about 1.05, inside the spec. Rf scaled down by 10× (to about 123 Ω) would also fit the spec, so Rf is the second candidate.
